metaTitle: What Does Digital Agency Mean? Definition
metaDescription: What does digital agency mean now? The label covers five very different businesses. Here's the definition, and the tells for which one you're calling.
answer: A digital agency is any firm selling marketing or product work delivered online. In practice the label covers five different businesses — performance media buyers, creative studios, web build shops, single-channel specialists like SEO, and generalists who claim all four. The term describes a delivery medium, not a skill.
takeaways: "Digital agency" tells you where the work happens, not what the firm is good at. It stopped discriminating the moment everything went online.
Five distinct businesses use the same label: **performance media**, **creative**, **web build**, **channel specialist**, **generalist**.
The fastest tell is what they ask you in the first ten minutes. A media buyer asks about CAC. A build shop asks about your stack.
Nobody licenses the term. A two-person shop and a 300-person network are equally entitled to it — and both are on somebody's "top 10" list.

sections.h2: Where the term came from, and why it stopped meaning anything
body: The label arrived in the late 1990s, when web and "interactive" work sat outside what traditional advertising agencies did. It was a genuinely useful distinction back then: those firms built websites, banner campaigns and email programmes, while the big agencies made television and print.

Then everything became digital. Television budgets moved to YouTube, print moved to search, direct mail became email and WhatsApp. By the time that shift finished, the prefix described almost the whole discipline — and a word that describes everything describes nothing.

So the term survived as a label of convenience. It's what a firm calls itself when it wants to be considered for any line in your budget. That isn't dishonest. It's just uninformative, which means the sorting work falls to you before the first invoice, not after.

sections.h2: Five businesses hiding behind one label
body: Almost every firm calling itself a digital agency is really one of these five. The differences show up in who they hire, how they charge and what their case studies measure. If you want the service-line view instead, we've written separately on [what a digital agency does day to day](/answers/what-does-a-digital-agency-do).

callout.title: The sixth type, which nobody advertises
callout.body: White-label resellers. They sell the retainer and subcontract the delivery, often to a production team in another city. It isn't automatically bad work — plenty of specialists earn a living this way. Not disclosing it is the problem, because you can't judge people you're never allowed to meet.

sections.h2: The tells that reveal which one you're talking to
body: Nobody will announce their type. They will, however, give it away within one call, because every agency asks the questions its own craft trained it to ask.

subs.h3: Listen to the first ten minutes
bullets: A **media buyer** asks what your customer acquisition cost is and how long payback takes.
A **creative shop** asks who you're for and why anyone should pick you over the cheaper option.
A **build shop** asks what you're running on, who owns the repo, and when the last deploy was.
A **channel specialist** asks for read access to Search Console or your ad account before the second call.
A **generalist** asks what your budget is, then shapes the answer around it.

subs.h3: Read the case studies for the unit of measurement
bullets: Launch dates, load times, uptime — build.
Rankings, qualified leads, revenue by channel — specialist.
Percentages with no baseline and no timeframe — nobody there is sure either.

subs.h3: Check how they want to be paid
bullets: A percentage of ad spend means a media buyer, and it means their income rises when your spend does.
A project fee with milestones means a build shop.

A monthly retainer with a deliverable list means a specialist or a generalist — [how a digital marketing agency works](/answers/how-does-a-digital-marketing-agency-work) covers where that money goes internally.
A day rate means a consultancy wearing agency clothing, which is fine if you wanted advice rather than hands.

sections.h2: Why the label predicts nothing about quality
body: There's no licence, no register, no exam. Anyone can incorporate on Monday, put "digital agency" on the site and quote on Tuesday. That's true of most professional services in India, but marketing has unusual cover: results are slow, attribution is contested, and a bad quarter can always be blamed on an algorithm update.

Badges don't fix it. Most industry awards charge an entry fee per submission, and most agency directories sell placement, sponsorship or leads. A badge proves a firm had a budget and somebody to write the entry.

Size doesn't fix it either. A 300-person network can put a 22-year-old on your account, and a two-person shop can be the best hire you make this year. What actually predicts quality is who does the work, which number they agree to be measured on, and whether they're willing to say no to anything.

callout.title: One question that skips all of this
callout.body: "Which of your last five clients would you not take again, and why?" A firm with a real filter answers in a sentence. A firm that takes anything with a pulse spends thirty seconds inventing something diplomatic. You'll hear the difference.

sections.h2: What to ask on the first call
body: Five questions, in this order. They take about twelve minutes and they save a month.
numbered: **Which of the five are you, really?** Read the list out and make them choose. Good ones pick immediately and tell you which parts they subcontract.
**Who does the work, and are they on this call?** A title instead of a name means you're buying hours from a pool.
**Which number do you want to be judged on?** Watch whether they reach for traffic and impressions or for qualified leads and revenue. It tells you what they're confident they can actually move.
**What do you refuse to do?** A firm with no refusals doesn't have a method. It has a price list.
**Do you subcontract any of this, and to whom?** Ask flatly. The answer is rarely the disqualifier; the hesitation is.

sections.h2: What we are, so you can sort us too
body: Last Agency is a channel specialist that runs three channels: [SEO](/seo), organic social and content, and performance media. We don't design brands, we don't build apps, and we say that on the first call because pretending otherwise costs everyone a month.

SEO starts at ₹75,000 a month, or ₹40,000 for smaller sites. Social runs ₹30,000, ₹50,000 or ₹70,000. Performance runs ₹40,000, ₹75,000 or ₹1,50,000. Bundles start at ₹99,000. All ex-GST, ad spend billed separately with zero media markup, month-to-month after the first quarter, and you keep every asset if you go.

We also take three clients a month, and that isn't scarcity theatre. We freeze your trailing-90-day qualified leads from organic search on day one and keep working free if we haven't beaten that number in 90 days. Nobody carries that risk across forty accounts. The full numbers are on the [pricing page](/pricing).

faqs.q: What's the difference between a digital agency and a marketing agency?
faqs.a: Increasingly nothing. "Marketing agency" is the older, broader term; "digital agency" signalled online-only work back when that was a real distinction. Today the difference is mostly which decade the founder started in. Judge on the service list and on what the case studies measure, not on the noun.

faqs.q: Is a digital agency the same as an advertising agency?
faqs.a: No. An advertising agency's core product is the idea and the media plan behind a campaign, usually with a production arm attached. A digital agency's core product is execution across owned and bought online channels. Large networks now sell both, which is exactly why the labels have blurred.

faqs.q: How big is a typical digital agency in India?
faqs.a: There's no reliable census and the range is enormous — plenty of Indian agencies are two founders plus a contractor pool, while network offices run into the hundreds. Ask for the size of your account team instead. That number is knowable, and it's the only one that affects your work.

faqs.q: Do digital agencies work with businesses of any size?
faqs.a: They'll all say yes. What actually changes is the retainer floor and who gets assigned to you. Below roughly ₹30,000 a month you're buying part of one junior's week, whatever the letterhead says. Ask what happens to your account in a month when a larger client escalates.

faqs.q: Does calling itself a digital agency mean the firm does SEO?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, and this is the most common mismatch we see. Plenty of digital agencies are paid-media shops that added SEO as a line item to hold the retainer together. Ask who on staff has done technical SEO, then ask to see a migration or an indexing fix they personally ran.
